description:
Measured on fz-sc8.171/qualified-macro-order e2ebcdf6f, interp, against elixir, with a range (1..3) and a MapSet as the enumerable. Thirty calls, each on both receivers; ten functions agree with Elixir (chunk_by, dedup_by, frequencies_by, group_by, max_by, min_by, min_max_by, sort_by, uniq_by, unzip). Twenty calls diverge:

Refused with error[spec/violation] because the @spec declares a list first argument (18): at/2, chunk_every/2, concat/1 (a list of enumerables), concat/2, count_until/2, dedup/1, fetch/2, fetch!/2, frequencies/1, join/1, join/2, max/1, min/1, min_max/1, product/1, sum/1, uniq/1, zip/2.

Missing (resolve/unknown-import): Enum.zip/1, Enum.zip_with/3.

Spiked: changing the spec domain from [a] to Enumerable.t(a) on join/1, join/2 and sum/1 alone makes all six probes print Elixir s output on interp and run ("123", "1-2-3", 6). The bodies already go through to_list or reduce. Not measured: build, the other fifteen, and the effect on the distiller compile-spend pin in tests/distill_telemetry_test.rs (49_760, 51_196, 28; 240 requests of headroom). Measure the pin before and after; a rise needs the user.

Build: for each of the eighteen, widen the domain and confirm the body handles a non-list; add zip/1 and zip_with/3 (check zip_with/2 too). One fixture printing every function on a list, a range, a MapSet and a map, identical to elixir on interp, run and build.

Separate from fz-sc8.141, which is about a receiver type only some of whose members implement the protocol.

Probe files and results: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/b141/census/ (result.txt).
title: Enum's list-only functions take any enumerable, as in Elixir
